signal.title: CSP26751 - Delegates for International Energy Agency Technology Collaboration Programme
signal.description: Introduction and Summary of Requirements DESNZ is looking for experts in their field with a strong network of contacts across their industry to act as an Alternate Delegate for the following International Energy Agency (IEA) Technology Collaboration Programmes (TCPs): Lot 1 Energy Storage (ES) Lot 2 Heat Pumping Technologies (HPT) Lot 3 Photovoltaic Power Systems (PVPS) Lot 4 Industrial Energy-Related Technologies and Systems (IETS) Summary UK Shared Business Services Ltd (UK SBS), acting on behalf of the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ), invites proposals for the role of Alternate Delegate for provision of support to the International Energy Agency (IEA) Technology Collaboration Programme (TCP). UK SBS is managing this procurement process in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023 (PA 2023) and the Procurement Regulations 2024 applicable to this procurement procedure (as may be amended from time to time) (the “Regulations”). This is a Services Contract being procured under the Open Procedure. This procurement shall be split into 4 Lots as follows and for each Lot one Contract shall be awarded to the successful supplier(s). LOT 1 - Energy Storage (ES) LOT 2 - Heat Pumping Technologies (HPT) LOT 3 - Photovoltaic Power Systems (PVPS) LOT 4 - Industrial Energy-Related Technologies and Systems (IETS) Please state clearly which lot you are applying for in your submission in the bid title. The application must be submitted by an organisation for a specific individual within the organisation. This can be a company, university, NGO or sole trader. An organisation may submit bids for several lots, no single individual may be proposed for more than one Lot. For example, a Supplier may bid for all four Lots; however, a different academic or employee must be nominated as the lead representative for each Lot. Each lot will be assessed individually so please provide a separate application for each lot applied for (including declarations). Each lot will only be awarded to one bidder. Background The IEA works to ensure reliable, affordable and clean energy for its 32 member countries and beyond. Founded in 1974, the IEA was initially designed to help countries co-ordinate a collective response to major disruptions in the supply of oil, such as the crisis of 1973/4. While this remains a key aspect of its work, the IEA has evolved and expanded. It is at the heart of global dialogue on energy innovations. Technology Collaboration Programmes (TCPs) are independent, international groups of experts that enable governments and industries from around the world to lead programmes and projects on a wide range of energy technologies and related issues. TCPs currently cover topics related to: • Efficient end-use (buildings, electricity, industry, transport). • Cleaner fossil fuels (greenhouse-gas mitigation, extraction, supply, transformation). • Renewable energy and hydrogen (technologies and policies for deployment). • Cross-cutting issues (modelling, technology transfer, project financing). • Fusion power (safety, physics, materials, technologies). The 6,000 experts in the TCPs work to advance the research, development and commercialisation of energy technologies. The scope and strategy of each TCP is in keeping with the IEA Shared Goals of energy security, environmental protection and economic growth, as well as engagement worldwide. Depending on the TCP, activities may include: • Basic and applied research, technology development and pilot plants • Technology assessment, feasibility studies, environmental impact studies, market analysis, policy implications • Information exchange of research results and programmes • Scientist exchanges • Databases, modelling and systems analysis • Experts’ networks. More information on the IEA and the TCPs is available here: Technology collaboration - About - IEA. Each TCP typically has two Delegates who represent each country at the Executive Committee: a primary Delegate and an Alternate Delegate. Each TCP is its own entity and therefore have different methods for organising activities. The types of activities are, however, broadly consistent across the TCPs. The UK is currently participating in 28 TCPs. The Science and Innovation for Climate and Energy (SICE) directorate in DESNZ funds 12 of these. At this time, DESNZ is looking to appoint Alternate Delegates for 4 of these TCPs to represent the UK industry alongside the primary DESNZ Delegate: • Energy Storage - https://iea-es.org/ • Heat Pump Technologies (HPT) - http://www.heatpumpingtechnologies.org • Photovoltaic Power Systems (PVPS) - https://iea-pvps.org/ • Industrial Energy-Related Technologies and Systems (IETS) - https://iea-industry.org/ The UK also participates in Mission Innovation, which is the leading international collaboration platform on innovation hosted by the IEA. SICE currently coordinates input into the seven Missions of Mission Innovation. Where relevant to the programme of work of the IEA Technology Collaboration Programmes, alternate delegates should seek to join up activities and stakeholder engagement. Acronyms and terminology: IEA TCP International Energy Agency (IEA) Technology Collaboration Programmes (TCPs): multilateral working groups established by the IEA across 8 themes (Buildings, Electricity, Industry, Transport, Renewable Energy, Fossil Energy, Fusion Power, cross-cutting) IEA TCP Secretariat Organises the general TCP administration (requesting invoices, organising annual activities), liaises with the IEA and stakeholders DESNZ (Primary) Delegate Government representative in the IEA TCPs. Drawn from across technical and policy teams. Primarily responsible for administration and knowledge transfer within DESNZ, quality assessment of UK outputs to IEA, but can get more involved depending on expertise and resource. Alternate Delegate (AD) Experts in their field appointed through open competition. In charge of running the UK’s TCP activities and producing main outputs. DESNZ TCP Co-ordinator Oversees all the TCPs at a working level within DESNZ and is responsible for the procurement of DESNZ and Alternate Delegates, reporting of TCP activities for DESNZ governing procedures and any general admin tasks not specific to individual TCPs. National TCP Coordinator Oversees all UK TCP Activity across 28 TCP Programmes with UK representation. Facilitates engagement across TCP representatives and provides support on alignment between TCPs and policy. Tasks / Annexes Sub-tasks produced by TCPs, where members create working groups to produce reports, gather international data on technologies/policies/ business models, etc. Known variously as tasks, sub-tasks, working groups, and annexes in different TCPs, but referred to as ‘annexes’ for clarity in this specification. Operating agent Project manager or technical lead of an annex. In charge of defining the programme of work of the annexes, and ensuring delivery of outputs. Known under different terminology across TCPs, but used here for clarity. National Team A team of UK experts from industry, third sector and academia convened by the Alternate Delegate. ExCo Executive committee meeting which typically occurs twice a year (generally at least once in person). The role of Alternate Delegate has general tasks common to all TCPs. Additional opportunities such as active participation in annex work or chairing the TCP can vary and be shaped by the AD and DESNZ Delegate. All ADs are expected to be able to complete all tasks, and the general tasks below are considered a minimum requirement. The Programme of Work will vary by TCP and will be jointly agreed with the DESNZ Delegate. The minimum requirement is expected to correspond to 12 days per financial year, amounting to a total minimum time requirement over the maximum potential duration of the contract of 29 days. Lot LOT 1 - Energy Storage (ES): LOT 1 - Energy Storage (ES). LOT 1 - Energy Storage (ES) The Alternate Delegate for the Energy Storage TCP will support in ensuring the UK derives value from participation in the Energy Storage TCP. The Energy Storage TCP’s mission is “to facilitate integral research, development, implementation, and integration of energy storage technologies in order to raise the efficiency of all types of energy system and promote an increasing use of renewables over fossil fuels”. The TCP is an international community of policy makers, academics, and industry professionals working on all aspects of energy storage. This includes tasks on electrical, thermal, chemical, mechanical energy storage; integration of energy storage with energy systems; energy storage materials and components; and other related areas of work. Further information can be found here: Energy Storage Technology Collaboration Programme - IEA ES TCP Country Members: Austria, Belgium, Canada, China, Czechia, Denmark, European Union, Finland, France, Germany, Israel, Italy, Japan, South Korea, The Netherlands, Norway, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Turkey, United Kingdom, USA The general tasks are: • Represent the UK in ExCo Meetings. • Act as the primary liaison between UK industry and the TCP. • Prepare national annual reports for the IEA on the state of research, technology deployment, policy support and projects. • Manage and develop the National Team of interested experts, to coordinate tasks and knowledge dissemination. • Participate in and propose TCP tasks or annexes, which are working groups aimed at delivering a specific task or output, advancing the knowledge base of the relevant TCP area. • Knowledge transfer from the TCP to DESNZ through the DESNZ Delegate. • Prepare a short annual report summarising TCP activities for DESNZ’s monitoring and reviewing purposes in collaboration with the DESNZ Delegate. Aims and Objectives The primary aims of this commission are to ensure that: • The activities of the TCPs are fully disseminated to their respective UK industries and researchers. • The UK takes an active role in the participation, management and development of the TCPs and ensures their activities are beneficial for the UK. • Activities across related TCPs are joined up, to avoid duplication and maximise added value through collaboration. Lot LOT 2 - Heat Pumping Technologies (HPT): LOT 2 - Heat Pumping Technologies (HPT). LOT 2 - Heat Pumping Technologies (HPT) The Alternate Delegate for the Heat Pumping Technologies TCP will support in ensuring the UK derives value from participation in the HPT TCP. The HPT TCP is a non-profit organization working in the field of heat pumping technologies, i.e., all technologies where heat is lifted from a lower temperature level to a higher one, such as heat pumps, air conditioning, and refrigeration. Under the management of an Executive Committee representing the member countries, the programme carries out a strategy to accelerate the use of heat pumping technologies in all applications where they can reduce energy consumption, increase the use of renewable energy sources, and contribute to energy security and affordable energy for all – for the benefit of people, the environment, and a sustainable future. The main activities within the programme are to run collaborative research, development, demonstration, and deployment projects, to organise a triennial conference, and to perform communication through the Heat Pump Centre, the Projects, and the National teams. Further detail of the HPT TCP can be found here: https://heatpumpingtechnologies.org/ Participating countries are: Austria, Belgium, Canada, China, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, France, Italy, Ireland, Germany, Japan, the Netherlands, Norway, South Korea, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, the United Kingdom, and the United States. The general tasks are: • Represent the UK in ExCo Meetings. • Act as the primary liaison between UK industry and the TCP. • Prepare national annual reports for the IEA on the state of research, technology deployment, policy support and projects. • Manage and develop the National Team of interested experts, to coordinate tasks and knowledge dissemination. • Participate in and propose TCP tasks or annexes, which are working groups aimed at delivering a specific task or output, advancing the knowledge base of the relevant TCP area. • Knowledge transfer from the TCP to DESNZ through the DESNZ Delegate. • Prepare a short annual report summarising TCP activities for DESNZ’s monitoring and reviewing purposes in collaboration with the DESNZ Delegate. Aims and Objectives The primary aims of this commission are to ensure that: • The activities of the TCPs are fully disseminated to their respective UK industries and researchers. • The UK takes an active role in the participation, management and development of the TCPs and ensures their activities are beneficial for the UK. • Activities across related TCPs are joined up, to avoid duplication and maximise added value through collaboration. Lot LOT 3 - Photovoltaic Power Systems (PVPS): LOT 3 - Photovoltaic Power Systems (PVPS). LOT 3 - Photovoltaic Power Systems (PVPS) The Alternate Delegate for the PVPS TCP will support in ensuring the UK derives value from participation in the PVPS TCP. The PVPS TCP conducts joint projects in the application of photovoltaic conversion of solar energy to electricity. This includes tasks related to PV sustainability activities, reliability and performance, transport, off-grid and edge-of-grid PV, and building-integrated PV. The IEA PVPS programme aims to realise its mission through the following objectives: • PV technology development • Competitive PV markets • An environmentally and economically sustainable PV industry • Policy recommendations and strategies • Impartial and reliable information Country members: Australia, Austria, Belgium, Canada, China, Denmark, European Union, Finland, France, Germany, India, Israel, Italy, Japan, Korea, Lithuania, Malaysia, Morocco, the Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Solar Energy Research Institute of Singapore (SERIS), Solar Power Europe, South Africa, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Thailand, Türkiye, United Kingdom and United States of America. The general tasks are: • Represent the UK in ExCo Meetings. • Act as the primary liaison between UK industry and the TCP. • Prepare national annual reports for the IEA on the state of research, technology deployment, policy support and projects. • Manage and develop the National Team of interested experts, to coordinate tasks and knowledge dissemination. • Participate in and propose TCP tasks or annexes, which are working groups aimed at delivering a specific task or output, advancing the knowledge base of the relevant TCP area. • Knowledge transfer from the TCP to DESNZ through the DESNZ Delegate. • Prepare a short annual report summarising TCP activities for DESNZ’s monitoring and reviewing purposes in collaboration with the DESNZ Delegate. • Essential Lot 3 Requirements • Demonstrable expertise in solar PV technologies and the UK PV sector, and a strong understanding of PV deployment, policy, regulation and market developments in the UK • Ability to provide a strategic perspective on PV within the broader context of renewable energy deployment and the energy transition • Good understanding of key UK PV stakeholders across government, industry and academia • Ability to utilise relevant official databases and statistics to support reporting and analysis The following would be advantageous: • Access to commercial market intelligence and PV market databases. In addition, for Lot 3 (PVPS TCP) The Alternate Delegate is expected to participate in Task 1 (Strategic PV Analysis and Outreach): https://iea-pvps.org/research-tasks/strategic-pv-analysis-outreach/ Task 1 produces at least two reports or special events annually, highlighting key drivers and status of PV development in both IEA PVPS countries and globally. Current discussions focus on PV integration in mature markets including grid constraints, flexibility, curtailment, negative pricing, and the role of storage and demand-side measures. The Task also examines policy and regulatory challenges associated with PV deployment, supply chains, manufacturing competitiveness and the translation of technical evidence into policy and regulatory action. The core activities in this task are: • Attend twice yearly physical meetings. These meetings are the primary forum for discussion and decision-making, including agreement on deliverables, events and future activities. Each meeting is minimum 2.5 days. • Complete the annual national data collection exercise (PV deployment, market trends, costs, policies and grid integration) for the Snapshot of Global PV Markets and Trends in Photovoltaic Applications reports. • Review documents produced by the Task Other activities may include: • Participation to additional workshops in international conferences organized by IEA-PVPS Task 1 • Participation to the writing of additional reports. • Organising Task 1 meetings • Working with Task 15 Manager to organise and deliver an international workshop/seminar (virtual) on plug-in solar PV, including contributing to the preparation of any associated report or publication. Aims and Objectives The primary aims of this commission are to ensure that: • The activities of the TCPs are fully disseminated to their respective UK industries and researchers. • The UK takes an active role in the participation, management and development of the TCPs and ensures their activities are beneficial for the UK. • Activities across related TCPs are joined up, to avoid duplication and maximise added value through collaboration. Lot LOT 4 - Industrial Energy-Related Technologies and Systems (IETS): LOT 4 - Industrial Energy-Related Technologies and Systems (IETS). LOT 4 – Industrial Energy-Related Technologies and Systems (IETS TCP) The Alternate Delegate for the IETS TCP (known as Industry TCP) will support in ensuring the UK derives value from participation in the Industry TCP and a similar initiative called the Net Zero Industries Mission. IEA Industrial Energy-Related Technologies and Systems (IETS) Technology Collaboration Programme (TCP) (known as Industry TCP): IETS | An IEA Technology Collaboration Programme The Industry TCP is coordinated by the Swedish Energy Agency and was launched in 2005. The programme is now wide ranging, covering industrial symbiosis, biorefineries, electrification, reuse of waste heat, AI, resilience to climate change, and circularity. At bi-annual Executive Committee Meetings government appointed delegates meet from each country to review updates on latest developments and share updates on policy and industry in their countries. The objective is to allow countries to work together to foster international co-operation for accelerated research and technology development of industrial energy-related technologies and systems with main focus on end-use technologies. The work is organised in Tasks, which can be viewed here: Tasks | IETS Country members: Austria, Canada, Denmark, France, Germany, Italy, Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Sweden, Switzerland, UK; Sponsors (university or industry): Japan, Ireland, Finland, Spain, Belgium Mission Innovation – Net Zero Industries Mission (NIM): Net-Zero Industries Mission Mission Innovation is the leading intergovernmental platform for collaboration on Innovation, launched at COP21 by world leaders when the Paris Agreement was signed, recognising the need for innovation to meet Net Zero goals. Missions are public-private partnerships focused on progressing towards a 2030 goal through international collaboration. NIM’s goal is to develop and demonstrate cost competitive solutions for the efficient decarbonization of energy intensive industries by 2030. The mission was launched in 2021 and is relatively new, with room to shape the activities based on UK interest. Country members: Australia, Austria, Canada, China, European Commission, Finland, Germany, Republic of Korea, UK, Switzerland. Sponsors and partners include AFID, ARENA, AIT, CEM IDDI, UNIDO, GCCA, MPP, LinkedIn etc. The general tasks of the delegate are: • Represent the UK in the TCP ExCo Meetings (2x per year 1-2 days) and TCP Interim ExCo Meetings (2x per year 0.5 days), • Act as the primary liaison between UK industry and academia and the TCP • Prepare national annual reports for the IEA on the state of research, technology deployment, policy support and projects on industrial decarbonisation. • Manage and develop the National Team of interested experts, to coordinate tasks and knowledge dissemination, alongside the Net Zero Industries Mission. • Participate in and propose TCP tasks or annexes, which are working groups aimed at delivering a specific task or output, advancing the knowledge base of the relevant TCP area. • Knowledge transfer from the TCP to DESNZ through the DESNZ Delegate. • Prepare a short annual report summarising TCP activities for DESNZ’s monitoring and reviewing purposes in collaboration with the DESNZ Delegate. Aims and Objectives The primary aims of this commission are to ensure that: • The activities of the TCPs are fully disseminated to their respective UK industries and researchers. • The UK takes an active role in the participation, management and development of the TCPs and ensures their activities are beneficial for the UK. • Activities across related TCPs are joined up, to avoid duplication and maximise added value through collaboration.

Further detail of the HPT TCP can be found here: https://heatpumpingtechnologies.org/ Participating countries are: Austria, Belgium, Canada, China, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, France, Italy, Ireland, Germany, Japan, the Netherlands, Norway, South Korea, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, the United Kingdom, and the United States. The general tasks are: • Represent the UK in ExCo Meetings. • Act as the primary liaison between UK industry and the TCP. • Prepare national annual reports for the IEA on the state of research, technology deployment, policy support and projects. • Manage and develop the National Team of interested experts, to coordinate tasks and knowledge dissemination. • Participate in and propose TCP tasks or annexes, which are working groups aimed at delivering a specific task or output, advancing the knowledge base of the relevant TCP area. • Knowledge transfer from the TCP to DESNZ through the DESNZ Delegate. • Prepare a short annual report summarising TCP activities for DESNZ’s monitoring and reviewing purposes in collaboration with the DESNZ Delegate. Aims and Objectives The primary aims of this commission are to ensure that: • The activities of the TCPs are fully disseminated to their respective UK industries and researchers. • The UK takes an active role in the participation, management and development of the TCPs and ensures their activities are beneficial for the UK. • Activities across related TCPs are joined up, to avoid duplication and maximise added value through collaboration. Lot LOT 3 - Photovoltaic Power Systems (PVPS): LOT 3 - Photovoltaic Power Systems (PVPS). LOT 3 - Photovoltaic Power Systems (PVPS) The Alternate Delegate for the PVPS TCP will support in ensuring the UK derives value from participation in the PVPS TCP. The PVPS TCP conducts joint projects in the application of photovoltaic conversion of solar energy to electricity. This includes tasks related to PV sustainability activities, reliability and performance, transport, off-grid and edge-of-grid PV, and building-integrated PV. The IEA PVPS programme aims to realise its mission through the following objectives: • PV technology development • Competitive PV markets • An environmentally and economically sustainable PV industry • Policy recommendations and strategies • Impartial and reliable information Country members: Australia, Austria, Belgium, Canada, China, Denmark, European Union, Finland, France, Germany, India, Israel, Italy, Japan, Korea, Lithuania, Malaysia, Morocco, the Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Solar Energy Research Institute of Singapore (SERIS), Solar Power Europe, South Africa, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Thailand, Türkiye, United Kingdom and United States of America. The general tasks are: • Represent the UK in ExCo Meetings. • Act as the primary liaison between UK industry and the TCP. • Prepare national annual reports for the IEA on the state of research, technology deployment, policy support and projects. • Manage and develop the National Team of interested experts, to coordinate tasks and knowledge dissemination. • Participate in and propose TCP tasks or annexes, which are working groups aimed at delivering a specific task or output, advancing the knowledge base of the relevant TCP area. • Knowledge transfer from the TCP to DESNZ through the DESNZ Delegate. • Prepare a short annual report summarising TCP activities for DESNZ’s monitoring and reviewing purposes in collaboration with the DESNZ Delegate. • Essential Lot 3 Requirements • Demonstrable expertise in solar PV technologies and the UK PV sector, and a strong understanding of PV deployment, policy, regulation and market developments in the UK • Ability to provide a strategic perspective on PV within the broader context of renewable energy deployment and the energy transition • Good understanding of key UK PV stakeholders across government, industry and academia • Ability to utilise relevant official databases and statistics to support reporting and analysis The following would be advantageous: • Access to commercial market intelligence and PV market databases. In addition, for Lot 3 (PVPS TCP) The Alternate Delegate is expected to participate in Task 1 (Strategic PV Analysis and Outreach): https://iea-pvps.org/research-tasks/strategic-pv-analysis-outreach/ Task 1 produces at least two reports or special events annually, highlighting key drivers and status of PV development in both IEA PVPS countries and globally. Current discussions focus on PV integration in mature markets including grid constraints, flexibility, curtailment, negative pricing, and the role of storage and demand-side measures. The Task also examines policy and regulatory challenges associated with PV deployment, supply chains, manufacturing competitiveness and the translation of technical evidence into policy and regulatory action. The core activities in this task are: • Attend twice yearly physical meetings. These meetings are the primary forum for discussion and decision-making, including agreement on deliverables, events and future activities. Each meeting is minimum 2.5 days. • Complete the annual national data collection exercise (PV deployment, market trends, costs, policies and grid integration) for the Snapshot of Global PV Markets and Trends in Photovoltaic Applications reports. • Review documents produced by the Task Other activities may include: • Participation to additional workshops in international conferences organized by IEA-PVPS Task 1 • Participation to the writing of additional reports. • Organising Task 1 meetings • Working with Task 15 Manager to organise and deliver an international workshop/seminar (virtual) on plug-in solar PV, including contributing to the preparation of any associated report or publication. Aims and Objectives The primary aims of this commission are to ensure that: • The activities of the TCPs are fully disseminated to their respective UK industries and researchers. • The UK takes an active role in the participation, management and development of the TCPs and ensures their activities are beneficial for the UK. • Activities across related TCPs are joined up, to avoid duplication and maximise added value through collaboration. Lot LOT 4 - Industrial Energy-Related Technologies and Systems (IETS): LOT 4 - Industrial Energy-Related Technologies and Systems (IETS). LOT 4 – Industrial Energy-Related Technologies and Systems (IETS TCP) The Alternate Delegate for the IETS TCP (known as Industry TCP) will support in ensuring the UK derives value from participation in the Industry TCP and a similar initiative called the Net Zero Industries Mission. IEA Industrial Energy-Related Technologies and Systems (IETS) Technology Collaboration Programme (TCP) (known as Industry TCP): IETS | An IEA Technology Collaboration Programme The Industry TCP is coordinated by the Swedish Energy Agency and was launched in 2005. The programme is now wide ranging, covering industrial symbiosis, biorefineries, electrification, reuse of waste heat, AI, resilience to climate change, and circularity. At bi-annual Executive Committee Meetings government appointed delegates meet from each country to review updates on latest developments and share updates on policy and industry in their countries. The objective is to allow countries to work together to foster international co-operation for accelerated research and technology development of industrial energy-related technologies and systems with main focus on end-use technologies. The work is organised in Tasks, which can be viewed here: Tasks | IETS Country members: Austria, Canada, Denmark, France, Germany, Italy, Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Sweden, Switzerland, UK; Sponsors (university or industry): Japan, Ireland, Finland, Spain, Belgium Mission Innovation – Net Zero Industries Mission (NIM): Net-Zero Industries Mission Mission Innovation is the leading intergovernmental platform for collaboration on Innovation, launched at COP21 by world leaders when the Paris Agreement was signed, recognising the need for innovation to meet Net Zero goals. Missions are public-private partnerships focused on progressing towards a 2030 goal through international collaboration. NIM’s goal is to develop and demonstrate cost competitive solutions for the efficient decarbonization of energy intensive industries by 2030. The mission was launched in 2021 and is relatively new, with room to shape the activities based on UK interest. Country members: Australia, Austria, Canada, China, European Commission, Finland, Germany, Republic of Korea, UK, Switzerland. Sponsors and partners include AFID, ARENA, AIT, CEM IDDI, UNIDO, GCCA, MPP, LinkedIn etc. The general tasks of the delegate are: • Represent the UK in the TCP ExCo Meetings (2x per year 1-2 days) and TCP Interim ExCo Meetings (2x per year 0.5 days), • Act as the primary liaison between UK industry and academia and the TCP • Prepare national annual reports for the IEA on the state of research, technology deployment, policy support and projects on industrial decarbonisation. • Manage and develop the National Team of interested experts, to coordinate tasks and knowledge dissemination, alongside the Net Zero Industries Mission. • Participate in and propose TCP tasks or annexes, which are working groups aimed at delivering a specific task or output, advancing the knowledge base of the relevant TCP area. • Knowledge transfer from the TCP to DESNZ through the DESNZ Delegate. • Prepare a short annual report summarising TCP activities for DESNZ’s monitoring and reviewing purposes in collaboration with the DESNZ Delegate. The service provider will be expected to work with Key stakeholders across ophthalmic services within the central and West integrated health community, including all ophthalmology patients, service users and families/carers. signal.title: Coaching von Bedarfsgemeinsch.
signal.description: Der Magistrat der Landeshauptstadt Wiesbaden schreibt die Maßnahme "Coaching von Bedarfsgemeinschaften auf der Grundlage von § 16f Abs. 2 Zweites Buch Sozialgesetzbuch (SGB II) und dem hessischen Ausbildungs- und Qualifizierungsbudget (AQB) aus. Ziel der Maßnahme ist die Steigerung der sozialen Teilhabe und der beruflichen Integrations-chancen von langzeitarbeitslosen erwerbsfähigen Leistungsberechtigten (eLb) in Bedarfs-gemeinschaften mit Kindern, in der ein oder mehrere Erwachsene nicht erwerbstätig sind. Ziel ist es, die Verstetigung des Leistungsbezuges zu durchbrechen und Perspektiven für Eltern und Kinder zu entwickeln, die für Eltern und Kindern zu beruflichen Aussichten und Möglichkeiten der Existenzsicherung führen. Dabei ist ein wichtiger Ansatz die Armutsprävention: denn durch die Erhöhung der sozialen Teilhabe, gerade der Kinder, werden die Chancen auf eine erfolgreiche Bildungs- und Erwerbsbiographie erhöht, die wiederum die Risiken des Leistungsbezugs reduzieren. Die Bedarfsgemeinschaft soll auch bei der Organisation von Hilfen unterstützt werden, beispielsweise bei der Beantragung von Leistungen für Bildung und Teilhabe, Unterstützung bei der Suche nach einem Kinder-betreuungsplatz, Verweisberatung zur Schuldnerberatung, Familienkarte, Erweiterung der digitalen Kompetenzen usw.. Durch die individuelle berufliche und soziale Förderung der Teilnehmenden, die in einer Bedarfsgemeinschaft mit Kindern leben, sollen die erwachsenen Mitglieder der Bedarfs-gemeinschaft aktiviert werden, die Vereinbarkeit von Familie und Beruf verbessert und bei der Alltagsorganisation, Behördengängen etc. unterstützt und bestenfalls eine Arbeitsintegration herbeigeführt werden. Die teilnehmenden Erziehenden der Bedarfsgemeinschaften sollen sich ihrer Vorbildfunktion und Bedeutung ihrer sozialen und beruflichen Teilhabe für sich selbst und ihre Kinder bewusst werden. Die Teilnehmenden und deren Kinder sollen dauerhaft für Integrationsbemühungen und -aktivitäten gestärkt werden. Es wird erwartet, dass bei mindestens 30 % der Teilnehmenden aktiviert werden, indem sie a) Flankierende Hilfsangebote (nach §16a SGB II) in Anspruch nehmen b) Hilfsangebote für die Kinder und Jugendlichen zur Inanspruchnahme führen, die sich positiv auf ihre Entwicklung auswirken (z. B. BuT, Ferienfreizeiten, Sportaktivitäten, Verhinderung von Ausbildungsabbrüchen, berufliche Orientierung im Hinblick auf Ausbildung und Studium etc.) c) in zielführende, qualifizierende, arbeitsmarktorientierte Maßnahmen weitervermittelt werden d) mit einem Minijob die Bedarfsgemeinschaft finanziell unterstützen 2.0. Zielgruppen Für die beiden Zielgruppen mit einer Förderung nach § 16f Abs. 2 SGB II und nach dem AQB werden die gleichen Leistungen "Beratung der Bedarfsgemeinschaft", "Workshops" und "Offener Treff" erbracht. 2.1. Zielgruppe der Förderung nach § 16f Abs. 2 SGB II Die Maßnahme richtet sich an langzeitarbeitslose, erwerbsfähige Leistungsberechtigte, die in einer Bedarfsgemeinschaft mit Kindern leben. Hierzu gehören auch langzeitarbeitslose nicht erwerbstätige Alleinerziehende mit Kindern. Die Zielgruppe zeichnet sich durch eine Arbeitsmarktferne aus. Es bestehen oft gesundheit-liche, sprachliche und häusliche Vermittlungshemmnisse. Der Zugang zu den eigenen Ressourcen ist beispielsweise aufgrund fehlender Erfolgserlebnisse verloren gegangen. Das "System Familie" ist eingefahren und braucht Unterstützung in der Balancefindung zwischen den verschiedenen, individuellen Schritten zur Verbesserung der Situation. Teilnehmende mit Migrationshintergrund sollten ein Sprachniveau von mind. A2 aufweisen, damit sie an den Workshops teilnehmen können. 2.2. Zielgruppe der Förderung durch das AQB Die Maßnahme richtet sich an erwerbsfähige Leistungsberechtigte, die in einer Bedarfsgemeinschaft mit Kindern ohne geregelte Kinderbetreuung leben und die Voraussetzungen des § 16f Abs. 2 SGB II nicht erfüllen. Die Zielgruppe zeichnet sich durch eine Arbeitsmarktferne aus und es bestehen oft gesund-heitliche, sprachliche und häusliche Vermittlungshemmnisse. Der Zugang zu den eigenen Ressourcen ist bspw. aufgrund fehlender Erfolgserlebnisse verloren gegangen. Das "System Familie" ist eingefahren und braucht Unterstützung in der Balancefindung zwischen den verschiedenen, individuellen Schritten zur Verbesserung der Situation. Teilnehmende mit Migrationshintergrund sollten ein Sprachniveau von mind. A2 aufweisen, damit sie an den Workshops teilnehmen können. Lot LOT-0000: Coaching von Bedarfsgemeinsch.. Die Beauftragung hat eine Laufzeit von 12 Monaten. Sie beginnt am 01.06.2025 und endet am 31.05.2026. Es bestehen zwei weitere Optionen zur Vertragsverlängerung um jeweils ein weiteres Jahr vom 01.06.2026 - 31.05.2027 und vom 01.06.2027 - 31.05.2028 Die Entscheidung über die Ausübung des Gestaltungsrechtes der Vertragsverlängerungen (Option) wird von dem Auftraggeber getroffen und steht nur diesem zu. Eine Unterbrechung der Leistungserbringung durch den Auftragnehmer über die gesetzlichen Feiertage hinaus, hierzu zählen auch der 24.12. und 31.12., ist ausschließlich an zwei Tagen zulässig. 3.2 Anzahl der Teilnehmenden, Coachingstunden, Workshops und Offene Treffs, Kinderbeaufsichtigung Während der Maßnahmelaufzeit ist ein Gesamtkontingent an Beratungsstunden, Workshops, Offene Treffs und Beaufsichtigungsstunden bereitzustellen. • Insgesamt sind 8580 Coachingstunden für das Coaching von Bedarfsgemeinschaften, finanziert aus § 16f Abs. 2 SGB II und AQB-Mitteln, anzubieten. Es werden bis zu 55 Teilnehmende die Maßnahme durchlaufen. Dies setzt sich aus 45 Teilnehmendenplätze mit bis zu 7020 Stunden finanziert aus § 16f Abs. 2 SGB II und 10 Teilnehmende mit bis zu 1560 Stunden finanziert aus AQB-Mitteln, zusammen. • es sind durchschnittlich vier Workshops pro Woche anzubieten, das entspricht 208 Workshops pro Jahr (davon 139 Workshops finanziert aus § 16f Abs. 2 SGB II und 69 Workshops aus AQB-Mitteln). Die Inhalte, der aus dem AQB finanzierten Workshops, sind unter Punkt 5.2 zu entnehmen. • es ist ein Offener Treff pro Woche anzubieten, das sind bis zu 52 Offene Treffs pro Jahr finanziert aus AQB-Mitteln. • Für die Beaufsichtigung der Kinder der Teilnehmenden der Bedarfsgemeinschaften sind bis zu 2016 Stunden Beaufsichtigung anzubieten, finanziert aus AQB-Mitteln. 3.3. Zeitlicher Umfang und Anforderungen an die Angebote Der Einstieg in die Maßnahme erfolgt zum 01.06.2025. Der Auftraggeber strebt die zeitnahe Nachbesetzung freigewordener Teilnehmerplätze bis zur maximalen Teilnehmeranzahl an. Der zeitliche Umfang der Maßnahme für alle Teilnehmenden umfasst: Coaching: Drei Zeitstunden Beratung inklusive Vor- und Nachbereitung pro Woche. Bei einer Laufzeit von 12 Monaten stehen pro Teilnehmenden durchschnittlich156 Stunden Beratung jährlich zur Verfügung, die flexibel, nach Bedarf der Teilnehmenden, einsetzbar sind. Da ein Beratungskontingent zur Verfügung gestellt wird, ist es möglich, innerhalb der verschiedenen Bedarfsgemeinschaften das Unterstützungsangebot zu variieren. Bedarfsgemeinschaften, die vorübergehend mehr Unterstützungsbedarf benötigen, können stärker zu unterstützt werden. Bedarfsgemeinschaften mit geringerem Bedarf dürfen auch mit weniger Beratungsstunden beraten werden. Dies erfolgt in Absprache mit dem Fallmanagement. Das Gesamtkontingent der vorgesehenen Beratungsstunden darf nicht überschritten werden. Workshops: Die Teilnahme an mindestens einem Workshop pro Woche mit drei Unterrichtseinheiten (eine Unterrichtseinheit entspricht 45 Minuten) ist für alle Teilnehmenden verpflichtend. Ein Workshop findet statt, wenn mindestens acht Teilnehmende für den Workshop vorgemerkt und eingeladen wurden. Der Bildungsträger plant die Workshops monatlich im Voraus und bucht die Teilnehmenden ihren Wünschen entsprechend in die Workshops ein. Workshops, die die geplante Mindestteilnehmendenzahl nicht erreichen, sind nicht förderfähig. Workshops, die die Mindestteilnehmendenzahl am Tag der Durchführung, beispielsweise aufgrund von Krankheit des Teilnehmenden, nicht erreichen, können mit dem Auftraggeber abgerechnet werden. Die Begründung für die Abwesenheit des Teilnehmenden werden vom Träger auf der Teilnehmendenliste dokumentiert. Bei voller Belegung des Förderangebotes sind pro Woche vier Workshops anzubieten. Sinkt die Anzahl der Teilnehmenden des Förderangebotes, ist auch das Workshopangebot zu verringern und entsprechend der Anzahl der Teilnehmenden anzupassen. Offener Treff: Der Offene Treff soll wöchentlich mit zwei Unterrichtseinheiten stattfinden, sowie einer Unterrichtseinheit Vor- und Nachbereitung. Der Besuch des Offenen Treffs ist freiwillig für die Teilnehmenden. Voraussetzungen zur Angebotsabgabe Nachweis der Leistungsfähigkeit: Der Umsatz in den letzten 3 Geschäftsjahren für vergleichbare Leistungen nach § 16 f Abs. 2. SGB II betrug durchschnittlich mindestens 400.000,00 € pro Jahr. Referenzen Mindestanforderung für den Bieter sind 3 Referenzen im Umfang von mindestens 30 Teilnehmenden in einem Geschäftsjahr für vergleichbare Leistungen nach § 16 f Abs. 2. SGB II innerhalb der letzten drei Jahre. Maximaler Auftragswert Der maximale Auftragswert beträgt insgesamt 1.910.000,00 €. Bitte berücksichtigen Sie, dass Ihr Angebot nur dann gewertet werden kann, wenn für die nachfolgend aufgeführten Punkte sämtliche Angaben gemacht wurden und der maximale Auftragswert nicht überschritten wird.

signal.title: Energie-Geschäftsreiseprogramm im Rahmen der Exportinitiative Energie des BMWE 2027, 2. Tranche
signal.description: Das Ziel der Exportinitiative Energie (EIE) des Bundesministeriums für Wirtschaft und Energie (BMWE) ist es, deutsche Unternehmen (UN), die klimafreundliche Energielösungen anbieten, beim Markteintritt im Ausland zu unterstützen und deutsche Produkte und Dienstleistungen international zu positionieren. Ein fester Bestandteil des Förderangebots ist das Energie-Geschäftsreiseprogramm. Ziel der Energie-Geschäftsreisen ist es, den Markteinstieg für deutsche KMU durch den Aufbau von fundierten Marktkenntnissen sowie die gezielte Kontaktvermittlung zu potenziellen Geschäftspartnern in den jeweiligen Zielmärkten vorzubereiten und bestehende Auslandsaktivitäten deutscher KMU weiter auszubauen. Das Fördermodul Energie-Geschäftsreise (GR) besteht aus einem Reisesteckbrief*, einer Zielmarktanalyse (ZMA*), einem Briefing vor Ort sowie einer Veranstaltung oder einer Kombination mehrerer Veranstaltungsformate*, die in Abhängigkeit von Zielmarkt und Themenschwerpunkt ausgewählt werden. Das zentrale Element der Maßnahme sind individuelle Gespräche der deutschen UN für eine gezielte Geschäftsanbahnung mit potenziellen Geschäftspartnern des Ziellandes. Lot LOT-0001: Los 1 - Bulgarien Nachhaltige Energieversorgung und Effizienzsteigerung in der Agrarwirtschaft. Zielland: Bulgarien Anwendungsfeld: Energieerzeugung Möglicher Termin: Q4 2027 Zielsetzung: Bei der GR soll die Identifikation und der Aufbau von Geschäftskontakten mit potenziellen Kunden im Zielmarkt im Fokus stehen. Daneben dient die Maßnahme der Darstellung der Leistungsfähigkeit deutscher Technologielösungen in diesem Bereich vor einem ausgewählten Fachpublikum. Der Aufbau von Geschäftskontakten soll im Rahmen individueller Kontaktgespräche erfolgen. Die im Leitfaden beschriebenen Vorgaben sind bei der Projektumsetzung anzuwenden. Die Veranstaltungsformate sollten so gewählt werden, dass die gesamte Bandbreite und Qualität deutscher Technologielösungen dargestellt und so das Ansehen der deutschen Unternehmen als führende Anbieter klimafreundlicher Energielösungen gestärkt wird. Dafür bietet sich die Organisation einer Fachkonferenz in einem der Zielländer an, zu der Branchenvertreterinnen und -vertreter aus dem zweiten Zielland eingeladen werden. Alternativ ist die Kombination aus zwei unterschiedlichen Formaten in beiden Zielländern möglich – dabei ist darauf zu achten, dass diese inhaltlich und konzeptionell aufeinander aufbauen und abwechslungsreich sind. Der Aufbau von Geschäftskontakten soll im Rahmen individueller Kontaktgespräche in beiden Zielländern erfolgen. Hinweis: Es soll eine regionale ZMA (Sonderversion) erstellt werden, die Estland und Lettland umfasst. Es sind zwei individuelle Potenzialanalysen zu Estland und Lettland zu verfassen. Die im Leitfaden beschriebenen Vorgaben sind bei der Projektumsetzung anzuwenden. translation.title: Energy business trip programme within the framework of the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy's (BMWE) 2027 Energy Export Initiative, 2 tranche
translation.description:
The aim of the Energy Export Initiative (EIE) of the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy (BMWE) is to support German companies (UN) offering climate-friendly energy solutions with market entry abroad and to position German products and services internationally. An integral part of the funding offer is the energy business trip programme. The aim of the energy business trips is to prepare market entry for German SMEs by building up sound market knowledge and targeted brokering of contacts with potential business partners in the respective target markets, and to further expand existing foreign activities of German SMEs. The energy business trip (GR) funding module consists of a travel profile*, a target market analysis (ZMA*), an on-site briefing and an event or a combination of several event formats*, which are selected depending on the target market and main topic. The central element of the measure is individual discussions by German UN for targeted business initiation with potential business partners in the destination country. Lot LOT-0001: Lot 1 - Bulgaria Sustainable energy supply and efficiency increase in agricultural economics. Destination country: Bulgaria Field of application: Energy generation Possible date: Q4 2027 Objective: The GR shall focus on the identification and establishment of business contacts with potential customers in the target market. In addition, the measure serves to present the performance of German technological solutions in this area to a selected specialist audience. The establishment of business contacts shall take place within the framework of individual contact discussions. The specifications described in the guidelines are to be applied during project implementation. Lot LOT-0002: Lot 2 - Estonia, Latvia Smart grids and energy storage for the integration of renewable energies. Destination country: Estonia, Latvia Field of application: Energy infrastructure and electromobility Possible date: Q4 2027 Objective: Building on a previous measure of the EIE on the technology focus, the GR aims to support German providers of innovative technologies for smart grids and energy storage in market development and consolidation in Estonia and Latvia. The event formats should be chosen in such a way that the entire range and quality of German technological solutions are presented and thus the reputation of German companies as leading providers of climate-friendly energy solutions is strengthened. For this purpose, the organisation of a specialist conference in one of the destination countries, to which industry representatives from the second destination country are invited, is suitable. Alternatively, the combination of two different formats in both destination countries is possible – care must be taken here to ensure that these build on one another in terms of content and concept and are varied. The establishment of business contacts shall take place within the framework of individual contact discussions in both destination countries. Note: A regional ZMA (special version) covering Estonia and Latvia is to be drawn up. Two individual potential analyses on Estonia and Latvia are to be written. The specifications described in the guidelines are to be applied during project implementation. Lot LOT-0003: Lot 3 - Greece Biomass and power-to-gas: Key technologies for decarbonisation and security of supply. Destination country: Greece Field of application: Energy generation Possible date: Q4 2027 Objective: The measure aims to position German companies in the biogas sector at an early stage in the emerging Greek market. The specialist event is intended to serve the dissemination of information and network formation and highlight the innovative strength of the German sector. The establishment of business contacts takes place within the framework of individual contact discussions. Note: The performance phase for the creation of a potential analysis is omitted. The specifications described in the guidelines are to be applied during project implementation. Lot LOT-0004: Lot 4 - Netherlands Security technologies for critical offshore energy infrastructure. Destination country: Netherlands Field of application: Energy infrastructure and electromobility Possible date: Q3 2027 Objective: The GR aims to accompany German providers in the aforementioned subject area in market development and consolidation in the Netherlands. In view of the specific topic, a careful definition of the target group to be addressed in Germany is to be undertaken. The selected event format should focus on the performance of German technologies and offer sufficient space for professional exchange in a trustworthy framework. A clear focus should be placed on the organisation of individual B2B discussions. Note: A longer ZMA is to be written (special version). The performance phase for the creation of a potential analysis is omitted. The specifications described in the guidelines are to be applied during project implementation. Lot LOT-0005: Lot 5 - Norway Decarbonisation of shipping and maritime infrastructure. Destination country: Norway Field of application: Energy generation Possible date: Q3 + Q4 2027 Objective: Building on hydrogen measures of the EIE in Norway in recent years, the GR aims to initiate partnerships between German and Norwegian companies. The specific technology needs in Norway in combination with a highly technologised market environment require an in-depth analysis of the local competitive environment and the German supply side in the run-up to the GR. The selected event format should emphasise the innovative capability of the German sector as well as enable professional exchange and access to decision-makers.

The focus of the GR is on the initiation of German-Norwegian cooperation, customer search for German products and services as well as the participation of German companies in specific projects in the destination country. Note: The GR is tendered in combination with a WEB. Participation in WEB is independent of registration for the GR. The aim is to inform German companies about the target market and the focal topic while simultaneously increasing the interest of German companies in participating in the upcoming GR. A longer ZMA is to be written (special version). The specifications described in the guidelines are to be applied during project implementation. Lot LOT-0006: Lot 6 - Hungary Energy infrastructure - Intelligent grids, digitalisation, energy storage. Destination country: Hungary Field of application: Energy infrastructure and electromobility Possible date: Q3 2027 Objective: The aim of the measure is to support German technology providers and service providers in market development and business initiation in the areas of electricity grid expansion, intelligent grids and energy storage in Hungary. A focus is placed on the presentation of the performance of German technologies and the establishment of business contacts with potential partners and customers using individual contact discussions. The selected event format should be chosen to suit the target audience and offer networking opportunities. The specifications described in the guidelines are to be applied during project implementation. Lot LOT-0007: Lot 7 - United Kingdom CCUS technologies for the decarbonisation of British industrial clusters. Destination country: United Kingdom Field of application: Energy generation Possible date: Q3 + Q4 2027 Objective: The GR aims to support German providers of CCUS technologies in building business relations with the United Kingdom. To this end, the framework of the selected event format should prioritise the presentation of the innovative strength of German technologies as well as professional exchange between German and British experts. The design of the event format should appeal to the local target audience and offer approaches for initiating concrete cooperation. The focus of the GR is on exploring concrete sales opportunities for German SMEs. For this purpose, a combination of individual cooperation discussions, visits to selected, ongoing projects with participation opportunities as well as exchange with British decision-makers is to be designed. Taking into account the most important industrial clusters that are the focus of British decarbonisation efforts and funding programmes, a sensible geographical orientation of the GR is also to be undertaken. Note: The GR is tendered in combination with a WEB. Participation in WEB is independent of registration for the GR. The aim is to inform German companies about the target market and the focal topic while simultaneously increasing the interest of German companies in participating in the upcoming GR. A longer ZMA is to be written (special version). The specifications described in the guidelines are to be applied during project implementation. Lot LOT-0008: Lot 8 - Argentina and Uruguay Energy efficiency and energy management in industry and buildings in Argentina and Uruguay. Destination country: Argentina and Uruguay Field of application: Energy efficiency Possible date: Q4 2027 Objective: The aim of the regional business trip is to provide German companies from the fields of energy efficiency and energy management in industry and buildings with targeted access to the markets in Argentina and Uruguay. The focus is on individually organised B2B discussions with potential customers and business partners in both destination countries. The aim is to tap into concrete business opportunities, build long-term partnerships and position German technologies and solutions in both markets. In addition, a specialist conference is planned in one of the two destination countries, at which German companies can present their technologies and solutions to a local specialist audience. In the second country, a networking event, for example in the form of a business breakfast, is to take place. Reasoned alternative event formats based on the attached guidelines can be taken into account. Site visits are not desired within the framework of the business trip. Note: A regional ZMA (special version) covering Argentina and Uruguay is to be created. The performance phase for the creation of a potential analysis is omitted. The specifications described in the guidelines are to be applied during project implementation. Lot LOT-0009: Lot 9 - Brazil and Paraguay Expansion of transmission grids, regional grid integration and resilient grid infrastructure. Destination country: Brazil and Paraguay Field of application: Energy infrastructure and electromobility Possible date: Q3 2027 Objective: The aim of the regional business trip is to provide German companies from the fields of energy infrastructure, transmission grids, grid modernisation and smart grid solutions with targeted access to business opportunities in Brazil and Paraguay. The focus is on individually organised B2B discussions with potential customers and business partners in both destination countries. In addition, targeted exchange with decision-makers from public institutions and the economy as well as with actors involved in the planning and development of major projects is to be promoted. In addition, suitable networking and dialogue formats are intended to support networking and deepened professional exchange between German companies and relevant actors in the energy markets of both countries.

Note: A regional ZMA (special version) covering Brazil and Paraguay is to be drawn up. The service phase for drawing up a potential analysis does not apply to Brazil. Only a potential analysis for Paraguay is to be drawn up. The specifications described in the guidelines must be applied during project implementation. Lot LOT-0010: Lot 10 - Brazil Biogas, biomethane and hydrogen in the energy sector in Brazil. Target country: Brazil Application area: Power generation Possible date: Q4 2027 Objective: The objective of the business trip is to facilitate access to the Brazilian market for German companies from the biogas, biomethane and hydrogen sectors, to identify specific business opportunities and to build sustainable business relationships. The focus is on individually organised discussions with potential business partners. If required, contacts with local financing institutions are also to be arranged in order to explore financing options for projects. A specialist conference is intended to promote knowledge transfer and technical exchange with Brazilian experts as well as relevant decision-makers from business, science and institutions, and to give German companies the opportunity to present their solutions. If implemented in several regions of Brazil, suitable exchange and dialogue formats, such as workshops, roundtables or networking events, can be provided as a supplement. Site visits are only planned in justified exceptional cases, provided they demonstrably support business initiation. Note: The service phase for drawing up a potential analysis does not apply. The specifications described in the guidelines must be applied during project implementation. Lot LOT-0011: Lot 11 - Costa Rica, Panama, Dominican Republic Technologies for energy efficiency in residential and commercial buildings. Target country: Costa Rica, Panama, Dominican Republic Application area: Energy efficiency Possible date: Q3 2027 Objective: The objective of the regional business trip is to facilitate access to new markets for German companies from the energy efficiency and self-supply sectors for industrial and commercial applications and to initiate specific business relationships. The focus is on individually organised B2B meetings with potential customers and business partners in all three target countries. The aim is to open up specific business opportunities, build long-term partnerships and position German technologies in the target markets. A specialist conference is intended to promote knowledge transfer and technical exchange with relevant market players and decision-makers. In addition, a suitable exchange or dialogue format, for example in the form of a workshop, roundtable or networking event, can be held in another target market. If required, contacts with local financing institutions should also be arranged. Site visits are not desired as part of the business trip. Note: A longer regional ZMA is to be written (special version) covering Costa Rica, Panama and the Dominican Republic. Three individual potential analyses on Costa Rica, Panama and the Dominican Republic are to be written. The specifications described in the guidelines must be applied during project implementation. Lot LOT-0012: Lot 12 - USA Energy solutions for data centres in California and Washington State. Target country: USA Application area: Energy efficiency Possible date: Q3 2027 Objective: The objective of the business trip is to facilitate access to the markets in California and Washington State for German companies, to open up specific business opportunities and to build long-term business relationships. The focus is on individually organised B2B meetings with potential customers, business partners and other relevant market players. In addition, suitable networking and exchange formats are intended to promote direct contact with local companies, institutions and decision-makers as well as the establishment of a viable network in both target markets. Individual B2B meetings are to be organised in both federal states for the participating German companies. Site visits are not desired as part of the business trip. Note: A longer ZMA is to be written (special version). The service phase for drawing up a potential analysis does not apply. The specifications described in the guidelines must be applied during project implementation. Lot LOT-0013: Lot 13 - USA Grid infrastructure, smart grids and storage technologies in New York. Target country: USA Application area: Energy infrastructure and electromobility Possible date: Q4 2027 Objective: The objective of the business trip is to facilitate access to the market in New York for German companies from the grid infrastructure, smart grids and storage technologies sectors, to open up specific business opportunities and to build long-term business relationships. The focus is on individually organised B2B meetings with potential customers and business partners. In addition, suitable networking and exchange formats are intended to promote direct contact with relevant market players, institutions and decision-makers and to support the establishment of a viable network in the target market. Site visits are not desired as part of the business trip. Note: The service phase for drawing up a potential analysis does not apply. The specifications described in the guidelines must be applied during project implementation. Lot LOT-0014: Lot 14 - Cape Verde Hybrid power generation from renewable energies (incl. storage). Target country: Cape Verde Application area: Power generation Possible date: Q4 2027 Objective: The energy business trip is intended to facilitate market entry in Cape Verde for German SMEs from the fields of hybrid power generation from renewable energies including storage.

The focus is on establishing business contacts with potential partners and customers as well as positioning German technologies and services in the local market environment. The measure is intended to facilitate access to relevant decision-makers and highlight specific project opportunities. The event format of the business trip should enable a comprehensive exchange of knowledge and experience as well as promote direct contact initiation between the delegation and relevant decision-makers. The event should be designed on the basis of a clearly defined question in order to gear the exchange specifically to the relevant needs and cooperation opportunities. In this context, information on planned projects and the modalities for participating in tender procedures should also be communicated wherever possible. The specifications described in the guidelines must be applied during project implementation. Lot LOT-0015: Lot 15 - India Energy-efficient (system) solutions for the decarbonisation of key Indian industries. Target country: India Application area: Energy efficiency Possible date: Q3 + Q4 2027 Objective: The measure serves the purpose of positioning German SMEs with a focus, inter alia, on energy-efficient industrial solutions, hydrogen, decarbonisation technologies and RE integration in the burgeoning Indian industrial and commercial sector. In terms of content, the measure is intended in particular to focus on target market sectors that are the subject of dedicated public funding within India. A key focus is on presenting the performance of German technologies and establishing business contacts with potential partners and customers through individual contact meetings. The travel agenda including the design of the event format is to be aligned with this objective. The overarching concern of the measure is accordingly to create a framework for sustainable business relationships and to strengthen the visibility of relevant technologies and solutions from Germany. Note: The business trip is tendered in combination with a webinar. Participation in the webinar is independent of registration for the business trip. The aim is to inform German companies about the target market and the focal topic while at the same time increasing the interest of German companies in participating in the upcoming business trip. The Indo-German Energy Forum (IGEF) must be integrated into the preparation and implementation of the measure. The service phase for drawing up a potential analysis does not apply. The specifications described in the guidelines must be applied during project implementation. Lot LOT-0016: Lot 16 - Israel Energy efficiency in buildings – zero-energy and plus-energy houses. Target country: Israel Application area: Energy efficiency Possible date: Q3 + Q4 2027 Objective: The measure serves the purpose of positioning German SMEs with a focus, inter alia, on energy-efficient construction and refurbishment, building automation and building-integrated power generation in the dynamic Israeli buildings sector. At the outset, German company solutions and best practices are to be presented to a high-calibre target audience of institutional, political and corporate decision-makers. A key focus is on presenting the performance of German technologies and establishing business contacts with potential partners and customers through individual contact meetings. The travel agenda including the design of the event format is to be aligned with this objective. The overarching concern of the measure is accordingly to create a framework for sustainable business relationships and to strengthen the visibility of relevant technologies and solutions from Germany. Note: The business trip is tendered in combination with a webinar. Participation in the webinar is independent of registration for the business trip. The aim is to inform German companies about the target market and the focal topic while at the same time increasing the interest of German companies in participating in the upcoming business trip. The Indo-German Energy Partnership must be integrated into the preparation and implementation of the measure. The service phase for drawing up a potential analysis does not apply. The specifications described in the guidelines must be applied during project implementation. Lot LOT-0017: Lot 17 - Thailand Energy efficiency in the buildings sector incl. rooftop PV systems. Target country: Thailand Application area: Energy efficiency Possible date: Q4 2027 Objective: The energy business trip is intended to facilitate market entry for German SMEs from the fields of energy-efficient solutions and rooftop PV systems for the buildings sector. The travel focuses on targeted contact brokering and individual B2B meetings with potential customers, partners and relevant stakeholders in Thailand. The measure is aimed at German SMEs with solutions in the areas of energy-efficient building technology, rooftop PV systems, battery storage, energy management systems, monitoring/O&M as well as engineering and compliance services. Note: The Thai-German Energy Dialogue is to be integrated into the preparation and implementation of the measure. The service phase for drawing up a potential analysis does not apply. The specifications described in the guidelines must be applied during project implementation. Lot LOT-0018: Lot 18 - Vietnam Industrial and commercial storage, smart management and PV. Target country: Vietnam Application area: Energy infrastructure and electromobility Possible date: Q4 2027 Objective: The energy business trip to Vietnam is intended to facilitate market entry for German SMEs from the fields of industrial and commercial storage, smart management and PV solutions.

translation.title: New construction of the administration building of the Dithmarschen district administration as a Public-Private Partnership (PPP)
translation.description: Procedure under the German Public Procurement Ordinance (VgV) for commissioning an economic and a technical adviser for the preparation of a public-private partnership (PPP) implementation of the structural engineering project for the new district office building. The district of Dithmarschen intends to construct the new district office building on the plot of land "Im Grund" as part of a public-private partnership (PPP). Darüber hinaus sollen alle Teilnehmenden aussagekräftige Bewerbungsunterlagen erarbeiten, die sowohl dem Fallmanagement, als auch den Kunden zur Verfügung gestellt werden. Das Stellensuchverhalten und die Bewerbungsaktivitäten der Teilnehmenden soll verbessert werden. Die Vorbereitung auf Vorstellungsgespräche und weitere Kompetenzen zur Optimierung des Bewerberverhaltens müssen beinhaltet sein. Um diese Ziele zu erreichen ist ein fester Bestandteil der Maßnahme eine praktische Erprobung im Rahmen einer Maßnahme beim Arbeitgeber (Praktikum). Diese ist für alle Teilnehmenden verpflichtend. Darüber hinaus sollen alle Teilnehmenden aussagekräftige Bewerbungsunterlagen erarbeiten, die sowohl dem Fallmanagement, als auch den Kunden zur Verfügung gestellt werden. Das Stellensuchverhalten und die Bewerbungsaktivitäten der Teilnehmenden soll verbessert werden. Die Vorbereitung auf Vorstellungsgespräche und weitere Kompetenzen zur Optimierung des Bewerberverhaltens müssen beinhaltet sein.

signal.title: Konesali-infrastruktuurilaitteet 2026 (00737)
signal.description: DYNAAMISEN HANKINTAJÄRJESTELMÄN KOHDE Dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän (DPS) kohteena ovat konesali-infrastruktuurilaitteet (esim. palvelimet, tallennus-ja varmistuslaitteet, integroidut ratkaisut ja konesaliverkon laitteet) sekä niihin liittyvien lisätarvikkeiden ja palveluiden hankinta. DPS:n kohde on kuvattu tarkemmin osallistumispyynnössä ja sen liitteissä, erityisesti liitteissä "Dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän kohde" ja "Palvelut ja niiden vähimmäisvaatimukset". DPS:n keston aikana kaikki kiinnostuneet ehdokkaat voivat tehdä siihen osallistumishakemuksen. DPS on voimassa hankintailmoituksessa ilmoitettuun päivään asti, ellei sitä keskeytetä tai muuteta DPS:n voimassaollessa. Hansel Oy:n asiakkaat toteuttavat hankinnat DPS:ään hyväksyttyjen ehdokkaiden kesken DPS:n sisäisillä kilpailutuksilla, jotka voivat ajoittua DPS:n koko hankintavaiheen ajalle. DPS:n hankintavaihe alkaa perustamisvaiheen jälkeen 30.9.2026 ja päättyy DPS:n voimassaoloajan päättyessä. Hankintasopimukset voivat olla voimassa enintään 30.9.2032 asti. Edellä mainitusta poiketen hankintasopimus on muilta osin voimassa niin kauan kuin sen perusteella hankittuihin tuotteisiin hankitaan dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän kohteena olevia palveluita (esim. huolto- ja ylläpitopalveluita tai kierrätyspalveluita). signal.title: Particle Size and Shape Analyser
signal.description: Instrument for particle size and shape characterisation of natural and industrial granular materials. Lot 1: . Instrument for particle size and shape characterisation of natural and industrial granular materials e.g.: -Volcanic flow particles (ash, lapilli, pumice, scoria etc.) derived from pyroclastic density currents, fallout deposits, lahars and debris flows. -Industrial particulate materials relevant to construction. -Soils -Construction materials (concretes, mortars, lightweight aggregates, composites) -Agricultural amendments and granules (including Biochar) -Polymer/composite additives -Energy storage materials (electrodes, conductive carbons) Materials will range from coarse granules to fine powders, typically irregular, porous, low-density and black. Essential requirements (minimum) Measurement capability -Measures both particle size distribution and particle shape in one instrument or tightly integrated system. -Image-based technique (e.g. dynamic image analysis or equivalent) suitable for irregular, opaque, carbonaceous particles. -Provides at least: -Size metrics: equivalent diameter, D10/D50/D90, full distribution. -Shape metrics: aspect ratio, circularity/roundness, and at least one compactness/solidity/convexity parameter. Size range and performance -Usable size range: -Lower limit ≤ 1μm -Upper limit ≥ 5 mm -Capable of analysing polydisperse samples in a single run. -At least 50,000 particles analysed per standard measurement (for powders). -Repeatability better than 3 % RSD on D10/D50/D90 for suitable reference materials. Sample handling and dispersion -Dry dispersion unit for low-density, porous, angular powders and granules: -Controlled feed (e.g. vibratory feeder or equivalent). -Adjustable dispersion energy/pressure. -Wet dispersion capability: -Recirculating wet cell for suspensions of soils, biochar and carbon powders. -Compatibility with at least water and common alcohols (e.g. ethanol or isopropanol). Shape analysis and classification -Shape parameters computed for all measured particles or size classes. -Ability to filter and analyse particles by size and/or shape (e.g. size range, aspect ratio range). -Display and export of representative particle images for documentation and publications. Software, data handling and reporting -Method/SOP editor for storing and recalling measurement conditions. -Export of size and shape data in standard formats (e.g. CSV, Excel). -Overlay and comparison of multiple measurements. -Configurable reports (number/area/volume distributions, cumulative and density plots, basic shape statistics). Calibration and practical aspects -Calibration/verification with traceable particle size standards in relevant ranges. -Documented traceability to relevant particle sizing standards (ISO/ASTM or equivalent). -Design suitable for dusty, abrasive, black powders, with straightforward cleaning of the dispersion path. -Enclosed optics and standard laser/electrical safety compliance. -Access to local service and technical support. 3. Desirable (nice-to-have) features Extended capabilities -Integrated laser diffraction module (wet and/or dry) using the same dispersion units, providing sub-micron coverage (≈0.1 μm or lower). -Dedicated fibre/rod analysis (length, width, L/W ratio) for fibrous chars/carbon fibres. -Extended upper size limit to ≥ 10 mm for large granules and aggregates. -Interchangeable optics/lenses to optimise measurements for fine powders vs coarse granules. Advanced dispersion and handling -Multiple dry disperser configurations (gentle and aggressive). -Integrated anti-static measures (e.g. ioniser) for very fine, low-density powders. -Low-volume wet cells (few mL) for expensive or low-yield materials. -Integrated, controllable ultrasonic dispersion (power and time) with logging. Automation and integration -Optional autosampler for unattended measurement of multiple samples. -API or scripting interface for method control and automated data extraction. -Database/LIMS connectivity for long-term storage and retrieval of results. Robustness -Wear-resistant materials in nozzles and flow paths. -Design that minimises cross-contamination.

signal.title: Cairngorms Peatland ACTION - Surveys for peatland restoration projects 2026
signal.description: The Cairngorm National Park Authority (CNPA) Peatland ACTION team are commissioning pre-application surveys and protected species surveys for planned peatland restoration projects within its operational area. Pre-application surveys are used to quantify the peat resource where the restoration is to take place, determine eligibility for grant funding, and inform design of the restoration works. The surveys will also provide baseline data for future monitoring of restoration outcomes and habitat condition. The data derived from the surveys and subsequent design work may be used by the landowner or their representatives for the purposes of Peatland Code registration. Protected species surveys are required to provide data to inform restoration design and identify potential ecological constraints. Detailed methodologies are provided for both survey types alongside this SOR. Lot 1: . The detailed schedule relates to the site(s), listed in the table 1 in the tender documents. Where multiple sites are listed consultants can bid for individual Lots or all Lots. If an individual Lot is bid for, all surveys and sites listed under that that Lot must be included in the bid. Maps of the survey area(s) are provided at the end of this document. High resolution maps will be available for surveyors with spatial data including site outlines and grid survey points where applicable (100m, HIA and 50m). There are hill tracks that access most of the survey areas however the survey will involve covering large areas of exposed, upland terrain off-road. Monie Mhor, Glenfeshie, also requires a ford crossing which may be inaccessible following heavy rain. Estate staff need to be contacted prior to the survey to arrange specific dates for access and to confirm any constraints present for each survey area. Contacts will be available from the CNPA following the contract award.

signal.title: Books and teaching aids for Troms County - RFI
signal.description: Troms County (hereafter called the Contracting Authority) shall enter into a new framework agreement for books and teaching aids. The procurement is now in a preparatory phase and needs mapping is currently being carried out, as well as examining the possibility that the contracting authority ́s total need for all types of books and teaching aids can be covered through a joint agreement. The contracting authority ́s need primarily includes access to teaching materials, textbooks and concretising materials connected to all disciplines and subjects in sixth form education and the vocational college. Furthermore, the contracting authority would like to be able to use digital books and teaching aids, as a supplement to printed books and teaching aids, as well as books available through NDLA. The contracting authority also sees the need for a contract for other types of printed books than teaching aids, such as entertainment and fiction books. Emphasis is put on the fact that the contracting authority has already entered into a separate framework agreement for e-books and e-audiobooks, and that such products are therefore exempt from this hearing. Question 1: As the first part of the market mapping, the contracting authority would therefore like to know whether there are actors in the market who can offer all types of products as mentioned above, including both printed and digital teaching aids for sixth form college and vocational college, as well as a wide range of fiction and entertainment books. The contracting authority envisages the following alternative options to cover the need: Through a joint framework agreement, by dividing the procurement into two sub-contracts; one for all types of teaching aids (printed and digital) and a separate sub-contract for fiction. By dividing the procurement into three sub-contracts; one for printed teaching aids, one for digital teaching aids and one for fiction. Question 2: We would like further market input on which of these three alternatives are feasible and which is best suited to safeguard the contracting authority ́s needs as described above. How should the hearing be answered? Response deadline Thursday 05 March 2026 (12:00). The hearing will be answered through the communication tab in Mercell. The inputs will be treated confidentially and not visualised for other suppliers. Please note that Troms County does not reimburse any costs for participation in the hearing. Once the hearing deadline has expired, we will carefully review all received inputs and assess what input it might be appropriate to include in the final documents. Emphasis is put on the contracting authority not be obliged to comply with the inputs. Tenderers who respond to this hearing may be contacted afterwards if needed for clarification or further questions. Furthermore, it may be necessary to send a draft of the competition documents for a hearing. We therefore recommend all interested suppliers to provide input for this hearing.
